transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-15 16:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Ortega (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Alex Kim (StudioForge CTO), Maya Patel (StudioForge VP Product), Jordan Reyes (StudioForge SRE)

[00:00] Jamie Ortega: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick intro, I'm Jamie, AE on the Redwood team, and Priya's our systems/infra SE. quick agenda: understand your constraints, the quickstart path if you want self-serve, and when Private or Dedicated makes sense.
[00:22] Alex Kim: Thanks Jamie. yeah, we wanna move fast, ideally a self-serve quickstart to demo to the product team. but security is a hard requirement, we handle PII in support transcripts.
[00:36] Maya Patel: onboarding needs to be fast, free credits help us get to first token quickly. our product goal is to add a chat surface and doc search within 4 weeks.
[00:49] Priya Nair: cool, that fits a typical PLG path. with Redwood self-serve you can get credits, get an API key, and be calling the Redwood API in a few hours — time-to-first-token is usually minutes once you have the key. for PII we talk through Private/VPC and also tokenization/encryption at the app layer.
[01:12] Jordan Reyes: can you clarify Private vs Dedicated vs hosted? we run in AWS, want minimal egress of sensitive data and company-managed KMS.
[01:26] Priya Nair: sure. hosted (Redwood API) is fastest to get started, we provide the control plane and runtime; Dedicated is reserved capacity — your own GPU pool managed by Redwood with stronger isolation and predictable latency; Private means customer-managed networking, VPC peering or our on-prem package so traffic stays in your network and you hold the KMS keys if needed.
[01:54] Alex Kim: are audit logs and SSO standard on Private? we need SAML SSO and audit trails for compliance.
[02:04] Jamie Ortega: yes, SSO/SAML and RBAC are available across Dedicated and Private; audit logs and extended retention are enterprise features we can include in a pilot. we'll attach the security brief.
[02:15] Maya Patel: how do credits work? we want to evaluate without committing to reserved capacity.
[02:21] Jamie Ortega: we commonly give free credits for a PLG quickstart — enough to run thousands of calls for an eval. credits apply to hosted usage; if you later move to Dedicated we can map eval usage into pilot planning and provide bridge pricing.
[02:36] Alex Kim: performance is critical. for our chat app, tail latency needs to be under 300ms for short responses, and cost per message matters. does Redwood do KV caching and batching?
[02:50] Priya Nair: yes, runtime supports prefix/KV caching, continuous batching, and quantization-friendly kernels. caching cuts a lot of token cost for repeated contexts. for latency we can route to lower-latency variants or dedicated nodes. there is a tradeoff: aggressive batching improves throughput and lowers per-token cost but can add latency; your SLO will determine the config.
[03:18] Jordan Reyes: do you have documented benchmarks on common models for 512 token sequences?
[03:24] Priya Nair: we have model profiles and perf numbers in the catalog; I'll share a spreadsheet and a simple latency worksheet. for pilot we can run a short benchmark on your sample prompts — we can reproduce in hosted or dedicated to compare.
[03:41] Alex Kim: ok, and data residency? we have EU customers so need to ensure logs and data are region-bound.
[03:48] Jamie Ortega: Redwood supports region pinning for hosted, and Private lets you keep everything in your VPC/region. we'll capture requirements and recommend a region strategy.
[04:03] Maya Patel: one concern - how often do model rollouts cause regressions? we want stability for the product.
[04:12] Priya Nair: good callout. Redwood provides rollouts, canary deploys, A/B test policies, and automatic fallback to pinned versions if a new variant regresses. also we tie quality regression alerts to prompt sets so you can guard rails before changing production models.
[04:30] Alex Kim: what's the integration surface? will this require changes to our infra or load balancers?
[04:36] Priya Nair: for hosted it's simply API calls over HTTPS; for VPC/private we set up peering or private link and a small agent or connector depending on on-prem. Jordan, you'd likely open a private peering and we coordinate security reviews.
[04:55] Jordan Reyes: agent? can you explain the on-prem package? we are air-gapped in some environments.
[05:01] Priya Nair: on-prem is an optional package, containerized, and can run without outbound internet if needed. there are a few extra steps for offline model provisioning and key management — we support HSM/KMS integrations.
[05:18] Alex Kim: cost model—do you charge per token for embeddings and generation? do you separate compute for dedicated?
[05:25] Jamie Ortega: hosted is usage-based per token and per-embedding unit, with transparent breakdowns. Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commits; we provide unit cost comparisons and suggestions in Optimize for quantization and batching to lower unit economics.
[05:40] Maya Patel: in terms of getting started, what do you recommend?
[05:44] Priya Nair: two paths: PLG quickstart — free credits, self-serve API keys, prototype within hours; or pilot with Dedicated/Private — we set up a short POC with predictable nodes and security add-ons. For your timeline (4 weeks), I'd start with PLG quickstart to validate UX and integration, then move to Private/VPC pilot for compliance.
[06:07] Alex Kim: would PLG quickstart allow us to test the end-to-end with our PII dataset? we can't send raw PII to a hosted provider.
[06:15] Jamie Ortega: right. for PII you can either pseudonymize or mask fields before sending to hosted. Or we can provision a Private pilot for a short term so keys and data don't leave your VPC. most customers do a hybrid: prototype in hosted with synthetic or masked data, then pilot Private with real PII.
[06:36] Jordan Reyes: what about encryption at rest and key rotation?
[06:40] Priya Nair: Redwood supports customer-managed keys for Private and Dedicated via KMS/HSM; key rotation policies are supported in the platform. for hosted we offer encryption at rest and can arrange KMS integrations for enterprise accounts.
[06:57] Maya Patel: are there constraints on inference frameworks or model types you support? we plan to use open models, maybe some finetuned variants.
[07:05] Priya Nair: we support common architectures and finetuned open models; the runtime picks optimized kernels and quant profiles. if you have a custom checkpoint we can onboard it through model onboarding process; that takes a little longer but it's doable.
[07:24] Alex Kim: what's the smallest pilot you do for Private? we don't want a large capex commitment, more like a 2-week private pilot.
[07:33] Jamie Ortega: we offer short Private pilots for evaluation; operational overhead is higher than hosted but we try to make it lightweight. typically a 2-4 week pilot with a small reserved node set and explicit rollback plan.
[07:51] Maya Patel: and who needs to be involved on our side?
[07:54] Priya Nair: product owner, a backend engineer to wire the API, and an infra/SRE for the networking and KMS bits — so Alex and Jordan will be key.
[08:07] Alex Kim: sounds good. how about SLA and support during pilot?
[08:12] Jamie Ortega: pilots get support via solutions engineering and a CSM during ramp; dedicated pilots can have an SLA. we'll include support details in the pilot proposal.
[08:23] Jordan Reyes: if we do hosted first then Private, how seamless is migrating API keys and models?
[08:30] Priya Nair: we try to keep the same API surface. you can pin model versions and rollbacks, and we can export model configs. there's some work to move data and keys for Private, but we provide a migration checklist.
[08:42] Maya Patel: any gotchas around rate limits and burst capacity? we expect spikes during demo days.
[08:49] Jamie Ortega: yes, hosted has quotas and rate limits; we can configure burst capacity. Dedicated offers predictable throughput and autoscaling policies, so for spikes Dedicated or Reserved plus autoscaling is better.
[09:05] Alex Kim: will you share a sample APM/tracing integration? we want request-level latency breakdowns.
[09:10] Priya Nair: yes, Redwood Console exposes per-route and per-model dashboards, tracing hooks, and error analysis. we'll share a short demo gif and docs.
[09:22] Maya Patel: timeline — if we accept the quickstart today, how soon can we be calling endpoints?
[09:27] Jamie Ortega: within hours: sign up, apply credits, get an API key, and call the Redwood API. time-to-first-token in practice is minutes once you have the key.
[09:38] Alex Kim: ok, I'd like to try a hybrid: prototype hosted with masked data, then run a short Private pilot for real PII. I'll need to see the security docs first.
[09:47] Jamie Ortega: perfect, we'll send SOC2, security brief, the pilot checklist, and sample pricing.
[09:54] Priya Nair: and I'll schedule the perf deep-dive to run benchmarks with your prompts and measure tail latency vs cost.
[10:02] Jordan Reyes: also include the network diagram and a sample peering checklist so I can see the infra changes.
[10:10] Jamie Ortega: absolutely. recap in bullet: we'll send security materials and pilot pricing, provide credits for hosted quickstart, Priya will run perf deep dive, and Alex will share sample PII flows.
[10:24] Maya Patel: thanks, that sounds like a good plan.
[10:27] Alex Kim: quick question, do you have reference customers in payments or healthcare who've done Private pilots?
[10:34] Jamie Ortega: yes, we can share references and anonymized case notes — I'll include a short list.
[10:41] Priya Nair: also note on cost optimizations: quantization and intelligent batching often drop unit costs significantly; for document search embeddings we can cache results and reduce calls.
[10:55] Jordan Reyes: thanks, that helps.
[11:00] Jamie Ortega: awesome, we'll follow up by Wednesday with the docs. thanks everyone.

[End of recording]

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-heard acronym "KV cash" instead of "KV cache" and speaker overlap around 04:00 - 05:00. Some proper nouns may be slightly off in the auto transcript.
